newsitem.title: USA: U.S. plans changes in CPI but many will take time.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plans changes in CPI but many will take time.

text.p: The Bureau of Labor Statistics plans to make some changes in the way the consumer price index is calculated, but many will take time, BLS Commissioner Katharine Abraham said on Thursday.
"We're looking to make changes as expeditiously as we can, she told reporters. "But I don't have anything in mind that at this point throwing more money at us would let us do faster.
"Money is not the only restraint here," she added. "It's skilled staff to do the work."
A Congressionally-appointed commission said Dec 4 that the consumer price index overstates the cost of living by 1.1 percentage points per year.
One change that the BLS will make next month regards the hospital component of the CPI, Abraham said. She was unsure though what impact that would have on the overall index.
The change will substantially broaden the number of items covered under the hospital component of the CPI.
In a paper explaining the changes, the BLS said it will also step up its efforts to obtain hospital transaction prices rather than hospital list prices.
"It's a step in the right direction," Abraham said. "I don't want to pretend it's a solution."
She said the BLS also plans to update the market basket weights within the index in January 1998.
